document.text:
A modular order-processing service separates the API component, order component, payment component, and database. The API component calls the order component through its published interface. The order component requires the payment component to authorize a purchase, and both components require the database to store durable state.

Dependency direction is constrained: the payment component must not call the API component. This separation prevents transport details from becoming part of payment logic. Published interfaces enable components to change internally without forcing callers to change, while direct access to another component's private data increases coupling.

The database is shared infrastructure, so a schema change can still affect both order and payment components. Keeping database access behind component interfaces decreases that coupling but adds implementation work and may make cross-component queries slower.

entities.description: An interface through which a component exposes functionality to other components.

entities.name: Durable state
entities.description: Persistent state stored in the database.

entities.name: Dependency direction

entities.name: Private data
entities.description: Data owned internally by another component and not exposed through its interface.

entities.name: Coupling
entities.description: The degree of dependency between components.

entities.name: Database schema change
entities.description: A change to the structure of the shared database schema.

entities.name: Database access behind component interfaces
entities.description: An arrangement in which components access the database through component interfaces rather than directly.

entities.name: Cross-component query
entities.description: A query involving data across component boundaries.

entities.name: Implementation work
entities.description: Additional work required to keep database access behind component interfaces.

entities.name: Cross-component query speed
entities.description: The speed of queries spanning component boundaries.
